events.title: Mayflower passengers sign the Mayflower Compact
events.description: Anchored off Cape Cod, 41 male passengers of the Mayflower signed a compact binding themselves into a 'civil body politic'. The agreement became an early landmark of self-government by consent in English America.
events.html: Anchored off Cape Cod, 41 male passengers of the Mayflower signed a compact binding themselves into a 'civil body politic'. The agreement became an early landmark of self-government by consent in English America.

events.title: Two Frenchmen make the first free flight in a balloon
events.description: Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes rose from the Bois de Boulogne in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon and drifted about 9 kilometres across Paris in 25 minutes, the first untethered human flight.
events.html: Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes rose from the Bois de Boulogne in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon and drifted about 9 kilometres across Paris in 25 minutes, the first untethered human flight.

events.title: Edison announces his phonograph
events.description: Thomas Edison announced his invention of the phonograph, a machine that recorded sound on tinfoil and played it back. It was the first device able to reproduce the human voice.
events.html: Thomas Edison announced his invention of the phonograph, a machine that recorded sound on tinfoil and played it back. It was the first device able to reproduce the human voice.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Dublin
events.description: Michael Collins's IRA squad killed 14 men, mostly British intelligence officers, in Dublin that morning. In the afternoon, Crown forces fired on the crowd at a Gaelic football match in Croke Park, killing 14 civilians.
events.html: Michael Collins's IRA squad killed 14 men, mostly British intelligence officers, in Dublin that morning. In the afternoon, Crown forces fired on the crowd at a Gaelic football match in Croke Park, killing 14 civilians.

events.title: The Dayton Agreement is initialled, ending the Bosnian War
events.description: After three weeks of talks at an air base in Ohio, the leaders of Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia initialled a peace agreement. The war had killed about 100,000 people, including some 8,000 at Srebrenica.
